PREFACE TO VOLUME II.

This Glossary of the Tribes and Castes found in the Panjab,
the North-West Frontier Province and the Protected Territories
| on the North-West Frontier of India, is basod upon the works of
the Inte Sir Denzil Charles Jelf Ibbotson, K-C.S.1, Lientonant-
MGovernor of the Punjab ani its Dependencies, and of the
Hon'ble Mr. Edward Douglas Maclagan, C.S.1., now Secretary
tothe Government of India in the Revenue Department. Sir
Denzil Ibbetson’s Report on the Punjab Census’ of 1881 was
reprinted as Punjiah Behnography, Volume ET of the present com-
pilation will include tho rest of this @oseary, and Volume I will
comprise the valuable chapters of Sir Denzil Ibbotson’s Report
which deal with the Physical Description of the Punjab, its Reli-
gions and other subjects, supplemented by the matter’ contained
in the Hon'ble Mr. Maclagan’s Report on the Punjab Consus of
1891, and from other sources.

This Glossary embodies some of the materials collected in
the Ethnographic Survey of India which was begun in 1900,
tinder the schemo initinted by Sir Herbert Risley, K.CLE.,
G.8.1., but it has no pretensions to finality. ‘The compiler's aim
Thas been to collest facts and rocord them in the fullest possible
detail without formulating theories as to the racial elements which
haye made the population of the modern Punjab, the growth of
its tribes or the evolution of caste, For information regard-
ing the various theories which have been suggested on those
topics the reader may be referred to the works of Sir Alexandet
Cunningham,* Bellew and Nesfield.;

The Census Report for Iudia, 1903, and The Races of India
misy also be referred to as standard works on these subjects.

It is in contemplation to add to Volume TIT, or to publish as
Volume IV, a subject-index to the whole of the present work,
